title: Keysight EDA update at DAC 2026 - Semiwiki
gist: A DAC 2026 booth interview with Keysight EDA's Nilesh Kamdar covers the company's push into quantum design software, multi-physics/photonics tooling built on the ESI Group and Synopsys optical-systems acquisitions, an AI assistant and MCP-server support in ADS 2027, and RFPro's new certification on Intel 14A/18A-P — evidence of EDA vendors consolidating adjacent design domains (mechanical, thermal, photonic) and racing to bolt agentic-AI/MCP interfaces onto legacy point tools.

themes.theme: Keysight EDA's acquisition-driven expansion beyond core RF/EDA

insights.claim: Keysight EDA acquired ESI Group roughly two years before September 2026, and now uses that multi-physics technology to build digital twins of automobiles for crash simulation and to model mechanical stress from thermal effects in advanced IC packaging.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Signals EDA vendors extending TAM into mechanical/automotive digital-twin simulation adjacent to chip design — watch for cross-selling of multi-physics tools into automotive and advanced-packaging customers.
insights.locator: In multi-physics, Keysight EDA acquired ESI Group two years ago

insights.claim: Keysight EDA acquired the optical systems group from Synopsys roughly one year before September 2026, combining it with in-house silicon photonics development to offer Electronic Photonic Design Automation (EPDA) for photonic integrated circuits.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A direct data point on EDA industry consolidation in silicon photonics — Synopsys divested an optical systems unit that Keysight absorbed, relevant to tracking competitive realignment in the photonics-EDA tool market ahead of co-packaged-optics demand growth.
insights.quote: plus they acquired the optical systems group from Synopsys one year ago
insights.locator: Another multi-physics offering is silicon photonics design

insights.claim: Keysight's newly acquired PowerArtist product, originally from Synopsys, performs RTL-stage power estimation and was shown at DAC 2026 with new features including real application activity profiling, upgraded parallel processing, AI-based power analysis reporting, and physically-aware RTL modeling.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Another concrete Synopsys-to-Keysight asset transfer in power-analysis EDA tooling; useful for tracking which EDA point-tool categories are being divested/consolidated and where AI features are being layered onto legacy RTL power tools.
insights.locator: The newly acquired PowerArtist product from Synopsys

themes.theme: Optical interconnect and photonics push for data centers

insights.claim: Keysight's EPDA tooling supports end-to-end electro-optical co-design for optical interconnect formats including Linear Pluggable Optics (LPO), Co-Packaged Optics (CPO), On-Board Optics (OBO), and Near-Package Optics (NPO), letting engineers simulate the full photonics chain before production measurement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Confirms EDA tool vendors are building out simulation stacks specifically for the CPO/optical-interconnect formats data centers are adopting for higher switching speeds — a leading indicator of design-tool readiness ahead of broader CPO deployment.
insights.locator: Electronic Photonic Design Automation (EPDA) software helps teams design

insights.claim: Keysight EDA says data centers are moving to optical communications for higher speeds than copper switching, and its tools can now simulate satellite-to-satellite and satellite-to-earth laser optical communication links, with computationally heavy light-propagation (FDTD) calculations accelerated using NVIDIA GPUs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Another vendor confirming the copper-to-optical shift inside data centers, and another EDA workload tying compute demand to NVIDIA GPUs — relevant to both optical-component suppliers and GPU-accelerated EDA compute demand.
insights.quote: Data centers are using optical communications for higher speeds than copper switching.
insights.locator: Optical communication like satellite to satellite

insights.claim: A Keysight customer used its MultiPhysics (thermal, electrical, CFD) solutions to push fluid through micro-vias in an interposer to cool an RF chip whose efficiency was dropping as it heated from radiated power, achieving a 10dB performance improvement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A vendor-supplied customer anecdote (unnamed customer, unverified) illustrating micro-fluidic interposer cooling as a thermal-management technique for high-power RF/advanced-packaging designs; treat as a case study claim rather than an independently verified benchmark.
insights.locator: One customer had an RF chip that radiated power

insights.claim: Keysight's ADS 2027 release will connect to any AI/ML modeling framework via MCP server support, enabling multi-agent tasks with either a foundational AI model or open-source models chosen to keep token costs low, plus in-depth surrogate model creation for fast design turnarounds.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Another EDA vendor adopting MCP (Model Context Protocol) as the integration layer for agentic AI in chip design workflows, following a broader industry pattern — track MCP adoption as a standardization signal across EDA vendors (Synopsys, Cadence, Keysight).
insights.quote: ADS 2027 connects to any AI/ML modeling framework by supporting MCP servers enabling multi-agent tasks.
insights.locator: On the AI front there is a natural language assistant

insights.claim: Keysight's EDA Learning Assistant is a generative-AI chat feature trained on ADS product documentation, providing context-aware answers to help RF and high-speed engineers become more productive.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A documentation-grounded AI copilot is now table stakes for EDA tool vendors; useful for benchmarking Keysight's AI feature parity against Synopsys/Cadence copilots.
insights.locator: Their EDA Learning Assistant is a generative AI chat feature

insights.claim: During DAC 2026, Keysight announced its RFPro electromagnetic design software was certified for Intel's 14A and 18A-P process nodes, letting RFIC and mixed-signal designers simulate and optimize Intel-process designs before production; Keysight had previously announced support for Intel's EMIB-T silicon bridge packaging technology for chiplet designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A concrete EDA tool-chain certification milestone for Intel's leading-edge 14A/18A-P nodes — a leading indicator that Intel foundry customers now have qualified RF/mixed-signal design tools, relevant to Intel Foundry's external customer-readiness timeline.
insights.quote: the RFPro electromagnetic (EM) design software was certified for the Intel 14A and Intel 18A-P process nodes
insights.locator: During DAC, it was announced that the RFPro

insights.claim: Keysight's Cliosoft data/IP management tools (branded SOS) support AI-powered design workflows to keep data clean, connected, and contextualized, with a new release called SOS.AI expected by the end of 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Watch for the SOS.AI release by year-end 2026 as a checkpoint on Keysight's AI-native IP/data management roadmap.
insights.quote: Expect a new release called SOS.AI by the end of the year, stay tuned for details.
insights.locator: For data and IP management there's the Cliosoft tools

insights.claim: In 2026 Keysight added quantum design as a new EDA software application area, alongside its existing focus on high-frequency/high-speed digital, RF, and mm/uwave design (e.g. communication chips at 10GHz or 100Gbps).
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: An early, still-vague signal that a major EDA vendor is entering quantum chip design tooling — worth monitoring for follow-up product specifics rather than acting on yet.
insights.quote: One new area in 2026 is EDA software for quantum design.
insights.locator: For Keysight the application areas of focus
